subject: Re: Rights delegation and feedback acceptance plan
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@venturicorp.com>
Cc: contracts@venturicorp.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rights delegation and feedback acceptance plan

Olivia — attaching our latest redline of the order form (RI_Redline_OrderForm_v2.docx). Quick summary of the outstanding IP/productization items so legal has them up front: 

- Output ownership: Venturi requests assignment/explicit ownership of customer-facing output for productization. We can offer a broad, perpetual, nonexclusive license to use, display and distribute outputs generated from Venturi data but cannot assign model ownership or provide exclusive downstream title.
- Training / data use: Venturi is asking to opt in to having customer data used to further train Redwood models. Our standard is to require explicit opt-in for retraining and narrower telemetry sharing.
- Feedback license: Venturi wants a license to feedback-derived improvements; we propose scoped telemetry & bug reports only — any broad knowledge transfer that affects model weights will require separate terms.

Can you confirm your legal team's main redlines and whether Venturi has a deadline for contract execution? We're trying to map to the procurement calendar so we can propose an escalation path if needed.

Action items I think we need: 
- Your confirmation on whether Venturi will accept a nonexclusive output license vs assignment.
- Whether Venturi requires a retrain opt-in or expects re-use by default.
- Any list of required evidence for compliance (audit logs, data provenance) so we can prepare upload links.

Attachments: [Attachment: RI_Redline_OrderForm_v2.docx (58KB)]

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call this week.

—Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0137

From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@venturicorp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Venturi Legal <contracts@venturicorp.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rights delegation and feedback acceptance plan

Rishi — thanks for the redline and summarized points. We reviewed with procurement and outside counsel; high-level responses below and a couple of clarifying q's: 

- Output ownership: Venturi prefers assignment of output rights so we can fully productize without additional license checks. If assignment is not on the table, we will need an unconditional right to create downstream products and to sublicense to our affiliates and integration partners.
- Training / data use: We will only opt out of retraining if there is significant commercial burden; otherwise, our expectation is that SaaS providers retain the right to improve models using anonymized/aggregated customer inputs unless explicitly opted out.
- Feedback license: We can accept a narrowly scoped operational feedback license (fixes, small improvements) but will push for a covenant that prevents Redwood from using feedback to create a competing domain-specific model without revenue share.

We attached a short note from our counsel with their comments and rationale. Venturi's procurement is aiming to close the onboarding by July 9 — they have an internal launch on July 20 that depends on contract execution.

Would you be open to a 30-minute call on Thu 24th to run through the specific order form clauses? If legal prefers, bring proposed compromise language.

Attachments: [Attachment: Venturi_Redlines_Notes.pdf (22KB)]

Best,
Olivia
Director, Platform Integrations | VenturiCorp
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rights delegation and feedback acceptance plan — internal response

Team — looping in our legal view so we can come back to Venturi with something executable. Quick notes: 

1) Assignment vs license: Assignment of output ownership is a hard no for us — it exposes model IP and downstream rights. Proposed approach: offer a perpetual, worldwide, transferable, nonexclusive license to exploit outputs, including to sublicense to Venturi's customers and partners, but retain all model IP and derivative rights. This gives Venturi commercial certainty without transferring core model IP.

2) Sublicensing: we can permit sublicensing to Venturi's affiliates and named integration partners, subject to standard flow-downs (no reverse engineering, no model retraining without opt-in).

3) Training / retrain opt-in: offer a dual-path: (a) default = no retrain; (b) if Venturi signs an addendum (retrain consent schedule) we permit aggregated/anonymized telemetry to be used for retraining with extra commercial consideration. For procurement speed, surface the addendum as optional and provide a template.

4) Feedback license / competitive carveout: accept operational feedback license; reject any permanent prohibition on Redwood using aggregated, de-identified feedback to improve general-purpose models. However, we can agree to a carveout that Redwood will not productize a Venturi-specific model trained exclusively on Venturi's proprietary corpus without explicit commercial terms.

5) Evidence & audit: suggest we offer an operational evidence pack (audit logs, token-level telemetry, retention policy) and a SOC-2+ questionnaire. We should attach a short checklist for Venturi so procurement can validate quickly.

I'm attaching suggested compromise clause language for the order form (proposed_moderate_language.docx). Recommend Rishi: present licensing path + optional retrain addendum on the 24th call. If Venturi holds to assignment, we'll need to elevate to Execs for a commercial carveout/fee.

Attachments: [Attachment: proposed_moderate_language.docx (14KB)]

—Laura
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@venturicorp.com>, contracts@venturicorp.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rights delegation and feedback acceptance plan — mutual action plan

Olivia / Venturi team — thanks for the quick review and for the timeline. Per our call notes and internal legal guidance, here is a proposed mutual action plan to keep to your July 9 close target: 

1) By Mon 28 Jun: Redwood to send final order form with compromise language (per Laura's attachment) and a templated Retrain Consent Addendum. (Attachment: RI_Redline_OrderForm_v2.docx — clean + tracked).
2) By Tue 29 Jun: Venturi to confirm whether sublicensing to affiliates/integration partners is acceptable under the proposed license grant and to identify any named partners requiring explicit listing.
3) By Wed 30 Jun: If Venturi requests assignment instead of license, escalate to Execs (Rishi to coordinate) — we will provide a commercial proposal for exclusivity/assignment considerations.
4) By Thu 1 Jul: Venturi procurement to confirm SOC-2 evidence checklist items; Redwood will provision an evidence bundle and a sample retention policy.
5) By Fri 2 Jul: Finalize DocuSign link for signature; target execution by July 6 to allow operational onboarding.

Notes: 
- We will not provide model ownership/weights. The compromise language permits broad downstream use of outputs and sublicensing but reserves model IP and retraining rights unless an addendum is executed.
- For feedback, we will accept an operational feedback license and a carveout that protects Venturi-specific models from being productized without separate commercial terms.

Please confirm each bullet and the timeline so I can lock the procurement calendar. If this looks good, I'll share the DocuSign flow and pre-fill the signatory fields.
